build_check.description: The project launches with the headless command, exits with code 0, and produces no fatal errors. Returns 0 or 1; the rest of the score is multiplied by this gate.

requirements.description: The player runs and jumps through a side-view chamber with gravity and solid terrain collision: the character lands on floors and platforms, is stopped by walls, and its sprite visibly changes pose between standing, running, and jumping. Score 0 if the player is static, slides through terrain, or teleports between positions. Score 1 requires the mechanic to be presented in a visually authored context with real sprites or illustrated assets. Score 0.5 at most if the mechanic works but is represented entirely by programmatic shapes, solid-color fills, or default Godot widgets.

An attempt is a timed loop: a visible loop timer runs, the loop ends when it expires or when the player ends it early, a rewind effect plays, the player returns to the chamber entrance, and the finished attempt becomes a new echo. Score 0 if no loop ends, the reset is not tied to a loop ending, or no echo is created. Score 1 requires the mechanic to be presented in a visually authored context with real sprites or illustrated assets. Score 0.5 at most if the mechanic works but is represented entirely by programmatic shapes, solid-color fills, or default Godot widgets.

An echo replays its recorded loop exactly: in the next loop the echo takes the same route at the same pace and timing as the attempt it recorded, and once its recording runs out it stays frozen in its final position. Score 0 if no echo appears, or the echo drifts from the recorded path, jitters, or teleports. Score 1 requires the mechanic to be presented in a visually authored context with real sprites or illustrated assets. Score 0.5 at most if the mechanic works but is represented entirely by programmatic shapes, solid-color fills, or default Godot widgets.

An echo operates a device that the live player then uses: the echo stands on a pressure plate, the linked door opens or the lift moves, and the live player passes through or rides it. Score 0 if no echo triggers a device or the live player never benefits from an echo's action. Score 1 requires the mechanic to be presented in a visually authored context with real sprites or illustrated assets. Score 0.5 at most if the mechanic works but is represented entirely by programmatic shapes, solid-color fills, or default Godot widgets.

A paradox is enforced: when the live player blocks an echo so it can no longer follow its recorded path, the echo visibly glitches, a PARADOX screen stops play, stability drops, and the chamber restarts at its first loop with no echoes. Score 0 if blocking an echo has no consequence. Score 1 requires the mechanic to be presented in a visually authored context with real sprites or illustrated assets. Score 0.5 at most if the mechanic works but is represented entirely by programmatic shapes, solid-color fills, or default Godot widgets.

The first chamber is solved with one echo: the live player's first loop ends on the plate, a rewind happens, and in the next loop the echo holds the plate so the door is open while the live player walks through to the exit, followed by a chamber clear screen. Score 0 if the first chamber is not solved through an echo holding the plate. Score 1 requires content variants to be visually distinct with real authored art (different sprites, illustrated elements). Score 0.5 at most if variants exist but are represented by programmatic shapes, color swaps, or text labels without real asset differences.

The lift chamber is solved: an echo stands on the lift's plate, the lift visibly travels while the plate is pressed, and the live player rides it up to reach a high exit. Score 0 if the lift does not move, moves without its plate being held, or the player does not reach the exit by riding it. Score 1 requires content variants to be visually distinct with real authored art (different sprites, illustrated elements). Score 0.5 at most if variants exist but are represented by programmatic shapes, color swaps, or text labels without real asset differences.

The final chamber is solved and the vault opens: two different echoes stand on two separate plates at the same time, the exit door that needs both opens, the live player avoids the laser hazard and exits, and a victory screen follows. Score 0 if fewer than two echoes hold plates together, there is no laser hazard on the route, or no victory screen follows. Score 1 requires content variants to be visually distinct with real authored art (different sprites, illustrated elements). Score 0.5 at most if variants exist but are represented by programmatic shapes, color swaps, or text labels without real asset differences.

Failure is meaningful: touching the laser costs stability and restarts the current loop, reaching zero stability shows a defeat screen, and choosing retry resumes play without relaunching the application. Score 0 if hazards have no consequence or there is no defeat screen. Score 1 requires content variants to be visually distinct with real authored art (different sprites, illustrated elements). Score 0.5 at most if variants exist but are represented by programmatic shapes, color swaps, or text labels without real asset differences.

During play the HUD shows the chamber name, the loop timer, the current loop out of the loops allowed, the echo count, and remaining stability, and these values update. Score 0 if there is no gameplay HUD. Score 1 requires the information to be presented through themed, styled UI with real assets. Score 0.5 at most if readability relies on plain text, unstyled labels, or raw geometric shapes.

Echoes are visually distinct from the live player and from each other: translucent or tinted, numbered or color-coded, with a ghost trail or similar effect, and they remain readable when overlapping the player or each other. Score 0 if echoes look identical to the live player or become unreadable when overlapping. Score 1 requires the information to be presented through themed, styled UI with real assets. Score 0.5 at most if readability relies on plain text, unstyled labels, or raw geometric shapes.

Device states and links are readable at 1280x720: plates, doors, the lift, and the laser show obvious on and off states, and wires, matching colors, or link lamps show which plate drives which device. Score 0 if device states are not visible or links are ambiguous. Score 1 requires the information to be presented through themed, styled UI with real assets. Score 0.5 at most if readability relies on plain text, unstyled labels, or raw geometric shapes.

Screens outside play are styled and clearly labeled: whichever of the title, chamber intro, chamber clear (with loops used and vault progress), PARADOX, defeat, and victory screens appear have themed headings and next or retry prompts. Score 0 if no styled screen appears or screens are plain text on a flat background. Score 1 requires the information to be presented through themed, styled UI with real assets. Score 0.5 at most if readability relies on plain text, unstyled labels, or raw geometric shapes.

Overall art direction is coherent and fits an industrial sci-fi vault with time-distortion effects across chambers, echoes, devices, HUD, and screens. Score 0 if most visible elements are default shapes, raw controls, or mismatched asset packs. Score 1 requires strong visual harmony: consistent palette, typography, iconography, and effects across gameplay and UI. Score 0.5 at most if the game uses programmatic shapes (ColorRect, solid fills, or untextured geometry) instead of real illustrated or pixel-art assets.

Chambers look authored: tiled terrain with edges and fill, decorative props such as pipes, signs, lamps, and chains, a background layer, and a visual theme that makes the chamber recognizable. Score 0 if chambers are flat colored blocks. Score 0.5 at most if the game uses programmatic shapes (ColorRect, solid fills, or untextured geometry) instead of real illustrated or pixel-art assets.

Characters, devices, and transitions animate: the player and echoes animate when moving, and rewinds, echo trails, plate presses, door and lift motion, laser flicker, and screen transitions play over multiple frames. Score 0 if all state changes are instant snaps. Score 0.5 at most if the game uses programmatic shapes (ColorRect, solid fills, or untextured geometry) instead of real illustrated or pixel-art assets.

Menus and overlays are polished: intro cards, HUD panels, and result screens use themed fonts, panels, and art rather than default Godot widgets, with smooth transitions between screens. Score 0 if menus are default widgets or plain text. Score 0.5 at most if the game uses programmatic shapes (ColorRect, solid fills, or untextured geometry) instead of real illustrated or pixel-art assets.
